findings.title: Missing HTTP security headers
findings.description: The application does not send one or more recommended security response headers, leaving it exposed to clickjacking, MIME sniffing, and content-injection attacks.
findings.evidence: Missing header(s): Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Strict-Transport-Security, Referrer-Policy
findings.remediation: Add the missing headers (e.g. Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Strict-Transport-Security, Referrer-Policy) at the app or reverse proxy layer.
findings.exploit_proof: Evidence captured during scanning (non-destructive): Missing header(s): Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Strict-Transport-Security, Referrer-Policy

findings.title: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
findings.description: User-supplied input is reflected into the HTML response without encoding, allowing script execution in a victim's browser.
findings.evidence: Payload reflected unescaped via '?q='. Marker: kv7xss
findings.remediation: Context-aware output encoding, a strict Content-Security-Policy, and input validation.

findings.title: SQL Injection (error-based)
findings.description: A single-quote probe triggers a database error, indicating input is concatenated into SQL and the app is injectable.
findings.evidence: DB error signature observed: 'you have an error in your sql syntax' at http://127.0.0.1:39357/search?id=%27
findings.remediation: Use parameterised queries / prepared statements and an ORM; never build SQL by string concatenation. Disable verbose DB errors.
findings.exploit_proof: Evidence captured during scanning (non-destructive): DB error signature observed: 'you have an error in your sql syntax' at http://127.0.0.1:39357/search?id=%27

findings.title: Directory listing enabled
findings.description: The server returns an auto-generated directory index, exposing file names an attacker can harvest.
findings.exploit_proof: Evidence captured during scanning (non-destructive): 'Index of' page served at /uploads/

findings.title: Exposed sensitive file: /.env
findings.description: A file that commonly contains secrets or source metadata is publicly readable.
findings.remediation: Block access to dotfiles/backups at the web server and remove them from the web root; rotate any leaked secrets.
findings.exploit_proof: Evidence captured during scanning (non-destructive): HTTP 200 at /.env containing sensitive keywords.

findings.title: Admin interface reachable without authentication
findings.description: An administrative endpoint is reachable and returns content without an authentication challenge.
findings.remediation: Require authentication + authorisation on all admin routes, restrict by network, and change default credentials.
findings.exploit_proof: Evidence captured during scanning (non-destructive): HTTP 200 at /admin returning admin/dashboard content.
